Bug_Details:
Reported as "Invariant Call" by loop-hoisting.

We report this issue type when a function call is loop-invariant and hoistable, i.e.

the function has no side side effects (pure)
has invariant arguments and result (i.e. have the same value in all loop iterations)
it is guaranteed to execute, i.e. it dominates all loop sources

int foo(int x, int y) { return x + y;}void invariant_hoist(int size) {    int x = 10;    int y = 5;    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {      foo(x, y); // hoistable    }  }
Bug_Explanation: The function `foo` is called inside a loop with invariant arguments (x and y) and is pure (no side effects), making it a candidate for hoisting outside the loop. This function call is hoistable because the result is the same for every iteration and does not depend on the loop variable.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with a size of 10. The bug is triggered because the function foo is called inside the loop with invariant arguments and is pure, which should be hoisted outside the loop to improve performance. The test is designed to fail as the actual result will not match the expected result due to the invariant call bug.
